title: Versola — Antifraud
description: The antifraud module of auth: decisions and what enforcing would have changed, rules, challenges, the SMS budget, the event pipeline, velocity counters, lists, detectors and storage. Written for a shadow-mode rollout: read Decisions first. Alert rules for the same signals: dashboards/alerts/versola-antifraud.rules.yaml.

panels.title: Decisions / s
panels.description: Antifraud decisions taken by this service: one per request that was judged. Empty means nothing is being judged: the engine is off, or no request has asked for a code.

panels.title: Would be refused or challenged
panels.description: Share of decisions whose would-be action (what the rules decided) was not Allow: Challenge, Fake or Block. In shadow mode this is the number to judge enforcing by: near the real share of bad traffic is right, a large share of ordinary traffic means a rule or a threshold is too tight.

panels.title: Let through, would be stopped
panels.description: Share of decisions that were acted on as Allow although the rules decided Challenge, Fake or Block. That is shadow mode working: the request went through and the decision was only recorded. After switching to enforce this falls to 0 (a failed evaluation under `failure-action` aside).

panels.title: Evaluation failures
panels.description: Evaluations that gave no decision in the selected time range (timeout, error or tuning unavailable); `failure-action` was applied instead. Must be 0: any is red.

panels.title: Decisions / s by would-be action
panels.description: What the rules decided, whatever was done about it. Mostly Allow is healthy; Challenge, Fake and Block here are what enforcing would do.

panels.title: Share not allowed: would-be vs acted
panels.description: Share of decisions that were not Allow, by what was decided and by what was done. In shadow mode the second line is flat at 0 while the first shows what enforcing would change; in enforce mode they are the same line.

panels.title: Acted on / s by action
panels.description: What was really done to requests. In shadow mode it is all Allow. Side by side with the panel on the right.

panels.title: Would have been / s by would-be action
panels.description: What the decisions were. Compare with the panel on the left: the gap between them is what switching to enforce would change.

panels.title: Evaluation failures / s by reason
panels.description: Evaluations with no decision: `timeout` (the engine took too long), `error` (an unexpected failure), `tuning_unavailable` (the tuned settings were never read). Empty is healthy; any value is red, and `failure-action` was applied to those requests.

panels.title: Rules fired / s (enforcing)
panels.description: The ten rules that fired most, among rules that count towards the decision. A rule that fires on most requests is a rule that is too wide.

panels.title: Rules fired / s (shadow rules)
panels.description: The ten most frequent rules that only record (`shadow:<name>` in the decision) and take no part in it. Read these before making a rule count: a rule that would fire on ordinary traffic must not be promoted.

panels.title: Rules fired — share of decisions
panels.description: Each rule's firing rate over the decisions per second. Several rules can fire on one request, so the shares do not add up to 100%.

panels.title: Proof of work: solved
panels.description: Of the proofs of work that were answered, the share that were right. Real browsers solve nearly all; a low share is scripts guessing, or a difficulty a phone cannot meet.

targets.expr: (sum(rate(antifraud_challenges_total{namespace="$namespace", app_kubernetes_io_component="auth", kind="pow", outcome="challenge_passed"}[$__rate_interval])) or vector(0)) / clamp_min(sum(rate(antifraud_challenges_total{namespace="$namespace", app_kubernetes_io_component="auth", kind="pow", outcome=~"challenge_passed|challenge_failed"}[$__rate_interval])), 0.001)

panels.title: Proof of work: answered
panels.description: Of the proofs of work put to clients, the share that came back with an answer. The rest are clients that cannot or will not do the work (no script, a bot that gave up): that is the point of the challenge. Falls if real users cannot solve it.

targets.expr: (sum(rate(antifraud_challenges_total{namespace="$namespace", app_kubernetes_io_component="auth", kind="pow", outcome=~"challenge_passed|challenge_failed"}[$__rate_interval])) or vector(0)) / clamp_min(sum(rate(antifraud_challenges_total{namespace="$namespace", app_kubernetes_io_component="auth", kind="pow", outcome="challenged"}[$__rate_interval])), 0.001)

panels.title: Pause: paid
panels.description: Of the pauses imposed on clients that cannot answer a proof of work, the share followed by the request that completed it and got the code. Real people wait and come back; a low share is traffic that leaves.

targets.expr: (sum(rate(antifraud_challenges_total{namespace="$namespace", app_kubernetes_io_component="auth", kind="pause", outcome="challenge_passed"}[$__rate_interval])) or vector(0)) / clamp_min(sum(rate(antifraud_challenges_total{namespace="$namespace", app_kubernetes_io_component="auth", kind="pause", outcome="challenged"}[$__rate_interval])), 0.001)

panels.title: Challenges / s
panels.description: Challenges put to clients. Empty while no decision is Challenge, which in shadow mode is always: nothing is challenged until enforcing.

panels.title: Challenges / s by kind and outcome
panels.description: `challenged` is a challenge put to a client, `challenge_passed` a right answer, `challenge_failed` a wrong one. `pow` is the proof of work, `pause` the wait for clients that cannot do one. Empty in shadow mode: nothing is challenged until enforcing.

panels.title: Pass rate and answered share
panels.description: A challenge that people pass and bots do not has a high pass rate among those answered and a lower answered share. Both low at once means real users are failing it.

targets.expr: (sum(rate(antifraud_challenges_total{namespace="$namespace", app_kubernetes_io_component="auth", kind="pow", outcome="challenge_passed"}[$__rate_interval])) or vector(0)) / clamp_min(sum(rate(antifraud_challenges_total{namespace="$namespace", app_kubernetes_io_component="auth", kind="pow", outcome=~"challenge_passed|challenge_failed"}[$__rate_interval])), 0.001)

(sum(rate(antifraud_challenges_total{namespace="$namespace", app_kubernetes_io_component="auth", kind="pow", outcome=~"challenge_passed|challenge_failed"}[$__rate_interval])) or vector(0)) / clamp_min(sum(rate(antifraud_challenges_total{namespace="$namespace", app_kubernetes_io_component="auth", kind="pow", outcome="challenged"}[$__rate_interval])), 0.001)

(sum(rate(antifraud_challenges_total{namespace="$namespace", app_kubernetes_io_component="auth", kind="pause", outcome="challenge_passed"}[$__rate_interval])) or vector(0)) / clamp_min(sum(rate(antifraud_challenges_total{namespace="$namespace", app_kubernetes_io_component="auth", kind="pause", outcome="challenged"}[$__rate_interval])), 0.001)

panels.title: Refused / s by reason and mode
panels.description: Codes the SMS budget closed a range to: `cap` (sentPerHour reached), `conversion` (too few codes verified: entered, or passed by passkey). `shadow` means the code went out all the same and the number is what enforcing would refuse; `enforce` is a refusal that happened. Empty while the budget is off (the default).

panels.title: Ranges not tracked / evicted per s
panels.description: `not tracked`: a code to a new range went out unchecked because the table of ranges was full: the budget no longer protects that tenant, and it is a sign of an attack or a table too small. `evicted`: a range was dropped to make room. Empty is healthy.

panels.title: Events enqueued, written and dropped / s
panels.description: Every request leaves an event; a writer stores them in batches. Healthy: written follows enqueued, and dropped is empty. `throttled_shed` is the log giving way under load, `queue_full` and `write_failed` are lost events, `shutdown` is a pod stopping with a queue.

panels.title: Events dropped / s by reason
panels.description: Events the log lost. Empty is healthy. `queue_full` and `write_failed` lose statistics (the decisions themselves are not affected); `build_failed` is a request that could not be described.

panels.title: Event queue size
panels.description: Events waiting for the writer, sampled each time the writer takes a batch. Near 0 is healthy; a queue that stays high is a database that cannot keep up.

panels.title: Backlog growth: enqueued − written − dropped
panels.description: Events that entered the queue and were neither written nor lost after entering (drops before the queue, `queue_full` and `throttled_shed`, are not in `enqueued`). Around 0 is healthy; above 0 for long is a queue filling up.

panels.title: Buckets flushed / s
panels.description: Counter buckets this service wrote to the database so that every instance sees the others' counts. Follows traffic; flat at 0 under traffic is a writer that does not run.

panels.title: Velocity failures / s by what
panels.description: `flush` (writing counts), `load` (reading the other instances' counts), `prune` (removing old rows). Empty is healthy; while it fails the counts are per instance only, so a limit is looser by the number of instances.

panels.title: Keys tracked
panels.description: Keys (networks, devices, ranges, phones) held in memory on each pod. Grows with distinct callers and is bounded by `velocity.max-keys`; a pod pinned at the bound is being flooded with keys.

panels.title: Keys not counted or evicted / s
panels.description: `not counted`: requests whose key could not be admitted to a full table, so no counter limited them. Rare once a full table evicts by sampling; any value is a flood of distinct keys far above `velocity.max-keys` or a table too small. `evicted`: keys that made room for a new one; a steady stream is a flood of distinct keys.

panels.title: List hits / s
panels.description: Requests that matched a list entry, by list, kind of value and whether the entry is a `shadow` one (matched, enforces nothing). Written every 30 seconds, so it is stepped. A shadow entry that hits ordinary traffic must not be made enforcing.

panels.title: List and tuning refresh failures
panels.description: A refresh that fails keeps the previous lists or tuning (fail open), so nothing breaks at once but changes stop arriving. Empty is healthy.

panels.title: List snapshot age
panels.description: Seconds since the lists were last read successfully. A minute or so is healthy (the refresh interval). The dashed line is the alert: 10 minutes means the pod enforces lists that old, and a hung refresh moves no failure counter, so this is the only place it shows. Empty while lists are off.

panels.title: Tuning age
panels.description: Seconds since the tuned settings (mode, thresholds, weights) were last read successfully. A few seconds is healthy (the refresh interval). The dashed line is the alert at 10 minutes: a pod that old ignores a switch from shadow to enforce.

panels.title: Proposals created / s by kind
panels.description: List entries the detectors proposed (they never create one). Empty while the detectors are off (the default) or nothing looks anomalous; a steady stream is worth reading in the console.

panels.title: Detector and housekeeping failures
panels.description: A detector run that failed (it tries again next interval) or the removal of old proposals that failed. Empty is healthy.

panels.title: Counter resets / s by scope
panels.description: Resets of the velocity counters and the SMS budget made through the API (`velocity`, `budget`, `all`). Each is an operator forgiving someone; a burst of them is worth asking about.

panels.title: Counter reset failures
panels.description: A reset that did not complete: `delete` (removing the stored rows) or `poll` (an instance reading the resets). Until it does, that instance goes on counting. Empty is healthy.

panels.title: Event partitions ahead
panels.description: Days of the event log that already have a partition. Healthy is the number the service keeps ahead (a few days). Below the dashed line at 2 maintenance is failing; at 0 the events of the day are written to the default partition until its partition is made.

panels.title: Maintenance and rollup failures
panels.description: Creating and dropping event partitions (retried every minute) and rolling the log up into the statistics the SMS detectors read. Empty is healthy; a failed rollup is recomputed by the next run, so a single one is not an incident.

panels.title: Database latency, antifraud operations
panels.description: Every antifraud database operation together (event inserts, rollups, velocity, lists, proposals). Client side, so it includes the pool and the pooler.

panels.title: Slowest antifraud operations (p99)
panels.description: The five operations with the highest p99. The event insert and the rollup are expected to lead; one that was fast and is not is where to look.

targets.expr: topk(5, histogram_quantile(0.99, sum by (le, operation) (rate(db_client_operation_duration_seconds_bucket{namespace="$namespace", app_kubernetes_io_component="auth", operation=~".*antifraud.*"}[$__rate_interval]))))

panels.title: Failed antifraud database operations / s
panels.description: Antifraud database operations that did not succeed. Empty is healthy.
